title: How Late Payments Became A Permanent Problem
gist: Gavekal Dragonomics notes that China's chronic late payments to private suppliers, especially by SOEs and government bodies, persist despite repeated rules in 2020 and 2025 and a personal pledge by Xi, with evidence that arrears are still worsening (paywalled preview only).

insights.claim: Small and private-sector Chinese businesses have for years complained of being paid late by customers, particularly state-owned enterprises and government departments, making arrears a potent symbol of the quality of China's business environment for private firms.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Arrears weigh on private-sector confidence and cash flow, a drag on China's private investment and growth.

insights.claim: Beijing has repeatedly tried to fix arrears, with new measures following national rules in 2025 that updated 2020 rules, and Xi Jinping personally pledged in February 2025 to resolve the problem.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Persistent policy attention without results signals structural, not just enforcement, causes.

insights.claim: Despite the top-level pledges, evidence suggests the cycle of delayed payments continues and arrears are still getting worse, which is exactly the outcome Xi said must not happen.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat official arrears-clearance claims skeptically; watch private-sector credit and SOE payables data.
